findings.claim: B3 accepts a release exception by checking the comment's original OWNER author, H, package digest and expiry, without protecting the approved body against edits. A repository writer can edit someone else's comment: replacing an old owner waiver's H/digest/expiry satisfies the written predicate without a new owner decision. This can authorize an unaudited release. The related A+1 claim that updated_at == created_at proves 'never edited' also lacks a reliable edit-history predicate; equality of timestamps alone cannot establish immutability. The B3 bypass does not depend on same-second timing and is sufficient for P1. This is a new comment-integrity manifestation affecting the R4-08/R4-11 authority closures.

evidence.observed: B3 requires OWNER authorship and H/digest/reason/expiry, but no edit validation or independently protected body binding. A+1 equates equal created_at/updated_at with never edited.

evidence.observed: Repository writers can delete others' comments; permitted moderators/writers can edit them. REST returns the comment author and mutable body/timestamps, so original authorship alone is insufficient authorization for the current body. [GitHub comment moderation](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/managing-disruptive-comments), [issue-comment API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments#update-an-issue-comment).

findings.suggested_fix: In B3 and B4, bind the exact owner-approved authorization body and identity to evidence that delegated comment writers cannot rewrite. Use a trustworthy no-edit indicator/history check or independently protected owner authorization, not timestamp equality alone; reject missing, edited or unverifiable records. Define revocation/latest-record behavior without silently resurrecting obsolete authority. Q7/Q9 must approve the resulting authority boundary and future packet scope. Test a non-owner edit changing H, digest, expiry and activation generation; same-second edits; deletion/latest-record fallback; variable off/on and delete/recreate across restart; REST denial. Positive controls must accept a genuinely new owner authorization. Preserve full-on-unknown for A+1 and blocking-on-unknown for B3. Stronger validation may reduce availability when evidence endpoints fail; provision and test the read-only route on each consumer host before activation, without changing frozen PR1.

notes:
Round 4, independently reviewed; one P1 finding, no P0/P2/P3 findings. This verdict does not authorize implementation, merge, deployment or another review round.

ROUND-3 CLOSURES: R4-08's specific delegated variable off/on replay is fixed by the strict timestamp inequality under fresh, monotonically ordered server observations: true -> false -> false, including restart and delete/recreate. An owner record created in the same timestamp unit as the variable is rejected, which is conservative. However, the broader owner-only authority claim is not fully established: see new R4-19 about mutable authorization comments. REST documents updated_at for repository variables; field availability is not the problem. Its documentation does not establish a cross-resource causal-order guarantee or that every no-op PATCH advances the timestamp. B4 must measure ordering, no-op writes, parsing and freshness as well as field presence. No live variable was read or changed.
R4-18 is closed at plan level. A+5 covers all eight shards and uses sum(median paired differences)/sum(median off times). The previous 0% sampled-shard / 17.5% overall counterexample now estimates 17.5%; a heavy-shard example estimates 9.3458%, and controlled 0%, 4%, 20% cases are correct. These are synthetic estimator checks, not production timings.
